## End-to-end journey

- Discover supported protocol versions, server identity, core capabilities, and extensions.
- Send any request with explicit request-local version and client capability metadata.
- List and call deterministic token-bounded pm tools, prompts, and resources.
- Respond to input_required results and retry the original request with inputResponses.
- Observe request progress and opted-in list or resource changes without connection-local state.
- Run long operations through durable task handles and application-level pm cursors.
- Receive actionable structured refusals for unsupported versions, missing capabilities, invalid schemas, authorization failures, and expired handles.
- Verify the same journey against a packed and published installation.
As an MCP host or coding agent, I can discover pm capabilities and complete long-running context workflows through one current stateless protocol

An MCP consumer can discover versions and capabilities, invoke pm tools and resources, satisfy requested input, follow progress or task state, and resume at application-level handles without hidden connection state.

The journey is executable over real stdio and Streamable HTTP transports; No successful operation depends on initialize state, an MCP session header, SSE redelivery, or undocumented server memory; Every response is token-bounded, deterministic where required, and exposes recovery when information is omitted; Input requests, task updates, progress, subscriptions, cancellation, and ordinary completion preserve one consistent state model; The packed and published agent transcript passes for npm, npx, bunx, and MCP consumers
One predictable current MCP experience for agents and hosts
Specify the end-to-end user outcome that all protocol, transport, task, resource, and conformance children jointly deliver
Integrators need fewer bespoke pm adapters and agents receive compact explainable context through standard MCP flows
The existing MCP experience depends on an obsolete handshake and does not expose the latest discovery, MRTR, subscription, cache, or task contracts
